To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD4+ CTL, DC and GC are present in the salivaries glands of SS patients.

the CD4+ T cell population of the SS lesion is not homogeneous and includes a distinct subset of cytotoxic cells and a distinct population of DC, which are both involved in the immunopathogenesis of SS.

1) CD4+ cytolytic T lymphocytes (Tc1) are involved in the pathogenic process of primary SS; 2) CD4+ Tc1 cells are activated by the antigen presenting cells, the dendritic cells; 3) the dendritic cells are present in the salivery gland lesions and are responsible for the antigen processing and presentation; 4) the antigen processing and presenting function of dendritic cells is supported by the presence of germinal centers
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the immunopathologic process in SS lesions, and provides new information on the cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in this autoimmune disease.
the immunopathogenic mechanisms of SS.
the identification of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that lead to the pathogenesis of SS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the salivary‐gland lesions of SS patients are characterized by the presence of CD4+ CTLs, DC and GC structures.
the salivary lesions of SS are a complex process which involves the activation of both CD4+ T and B lymphocytes.

the immunopathological lesion of SS may be the result of a combination of the following events: (a) the formation of GC, (b) the presence of a CD4‐mediated cytotoxic T lymphocyte population and (c) the activation of DC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SS is a complex disease in which several immunopathologic mechanisms are involved in the development of the salivatory gland lesions.
the immunopathologic lesions of Sjögrens syndrome may be attributed to a combined action of both CD4+ T and B lymphocytes.

SS lesions contain a distinct CD4+ CTL population that utilizes perforins as the cytotoxic effector molecule, DC and GC structures that are probably involved in the activation and proliferation of T and B lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD4+ CTLs and DC may play a key role in the immunopathological process of SS.
the immunopathologic process of Sjögreen's syndrome involves the activation and proliferation of B lymphocytes, as well as the activation of CD4+ cytolytic T lymphocytes.
SS is a complex disease, with many different cell types involved.
